title: Legacy Agent Sunset & Conversion Playbook
content:
Summary:
This playbook covers the planned retirement (sunset) of the legacy on-prem agent and the safe conversion of private deployments to the new runtime-adapter architecture. It purposefully focuses on minimum-risk mechanical steps, Terraform module mapping guidance, compatibility shim behavior, and operator checklists for testing, rollback and post-cutover validation.

Goals:
- Remove legacy agent binary from customer appliance images without interrupting customer traffic.
- Provide a migration path that supports mixed clusters for a configurable co-existence window (default 6 weeks).
- Ensure API compatibility for management/control-plane interactions during transition.
- Keep SLOs intact (99.9% availability for serving RPCs, <5% p95 latency impact).

Scope and Assumptions:
- Applies only to private deployments (VPC and on-prem appliance).
- Customers currently running agent v0.*. New target is runtime-adapter v1.0 with sidecar shim.
- Terraform modules referenced: modules/agent, modules/runtime-adapter, modules/network. Customers using heavily modified TF forks will need extra manual steps (see appendix).

High-level migration phases:
1) Canary adapter rollout: deploy runtime-adapter sidecar to 2-3 non-critical nodes. Enable request mirroring from legacy agent to adapter (no traffic cut). Duration: 3-7 days.
2) Compatibility shim enablement: flip control-plane flag allow_adapter_ops=true. Adapter will accept management RPCs but forward to legacy agent for unmatched endpoints. Duration: 1 week.
3) Progressive conversion: convert 10% -> 30% -> 60% of nodes using TF blue/green mapping for instance groups. Keep automatic fallback to legacy agent. Duration: 2-3 weeks.
4) Agent sunset cutover: deprecate legacy agent in images and remove old TF module. Run migration validation and increase monitoring retention windows. Duration: 48-96 hours for scheduled cutover.
5) Post-sunset cleanup: remove shim code paths after 6 weeks, delete legacy module state, and run final audit.

Terraform module notes (practical mapping):
- modules/agent -> modules/runtime-adapter mapping checklist:
  - Replace resource "redwood_agent_service" with "runtime_adapter_service". Keep original service name tag for metrics continuity.
  - Move TLS certs into adapter_secret_id (adapter reads from KMS path).
  - If customer used agent.custom_env, pass through as adapter.env.CONTAINER_OVERRIDES.
  - For autoscaling policies, preserve min/max and copy scaling metrics; add adapter-specific metric adapter_queue_depth as a soft-signal.

- State migration guidance:
  - Create migration.tf containing alias resources that import existing agent resources into new adapter module (use terraform import with exact IDs).
  - Lock TF state during import window; smallest window preferred (target less than 15 minutes for large fleets).

Compatibility shim behavior (runtime-adapter sidecar):
- Default mode: passive-forwarding. Unhandled control-plane RPCs are proxied to legacy agent.
- Verification mode: logs every proxied call with header X-Adapter-Proxied: true.
- Strict mode (post-cutover): reject legacy RPCs with 410 and guidance URL in response.
- Safety toggle: adapter.env.FORWARDING_ENABLED=true|false controlled via secret manager.

Cutover safety checks (gate tests before each phase):
- Telemetry sanity: aggregated request rate for adapter vs legacy agent is stable within expected ratio after mirroring.
- KV cache parity: sampling of KV lookup keys returns identical values on adapter and agent for 500 random keys.
- Integration smoke: control-plane agents can list and describe nodes via adapter.
- E2E inference test: synthetic workload ~1k requests/min across p50/p95 latency checks.

Rollback playbook (fast rollback knobs):
- For TF-driven conversions: re-apply previous module config (terraform apply) using the preserved agent module and re-enable agent service. Keep adapter sidecar running in passive mode until stable.
- Control-plane flag rollback: set allow_adapter_ops=false to force managed traffic back to legacy agent.
- Image revert: redeploy previous golden image with agent installed (immediate).
- Network-level block: if adapter is misbehaving, firewall rule to drop adapter port egress to control plane to force legacy routing.

Observability and KPIs to monitor during migration:
- Adapter error rate (5xx) — threshold 0.5%
- Control-plane RPC latency (p95) — should not increase >10% vs baseline
- Token-billing divergence — tokens counted by adapter vs legacy must match within 0.2% over 24h
- Rollout alert: any sustained >2% user-facing errors for 15+ minutes triggers automated rollback policy

Operator quick reference (cheat sheet):
- Start canary: tf apply -var=instance_group=canary -target=module.runtime_adapter_service
- Enable forwarding: gcloud secrets versions add adapter-settings --payload="FORWARDING_ENABLED=true\nX=..."
- Validate KV parity: scripts/kv-compare.sh --sample 500 --adapter-endpoint=$ADAPTER --agent-endpoint=$AGENT
- Fast revert: tf apply -var-file=rollback.tfvars -target=module.agent_service

Testing matrix (minimum):
- Unit: adapter logic, proxy, certificate rotation handlers (CI)
- Integration: adapter <-> control-plane RPCs, shim proxying (staging cluster)
- Load: 3x expected burst for both legacy and adapter under mirroring
- Chaos: node restarts, transient network failures while mirroring enabled

Security and compliance notes:
- Adapter reads same KMS keys; rotate keys in a controlled manner (rotate adapter key first, then agent key after verification).
- Audit logs must preserve agent-origin field until final cleanup.
- Customers with HIPAA/PCA requirements: document the co-existence window and get signed approval to modify images.

Appendix A: Example terraform import steps (abridged)
- terraform init
- terraform state rm module.agent_service.redwood_agent_service.agent || true
- terraform import module.runtime_adapter_service.runtime_adapter_service.adapter-12345 adapter-12345
- terraform plan
- terraform apply

Appendix B: Common failure modes and remedies
- Symptom: adapter rejects certs from control plane -> Remedy: ensure adapter loads the same CA bundle and that certificate SANs include control-plane hostnames.
- Symptom: token counts diverge -> Remedy: enable debug-proxy and compare request IDs, pause new deployments and do bridge sync.

Owners and escalation paths:
- Migration PM: Priya Rao (primary contact)
- SRE lead: Ethan Zhao (runbook ops)
- Runtime eng: Diego Hernandez (adapter maintainers)
- Legal/Compliance: Ana Martinez (approvals for regulated customers)

Estimated timeline for a medium-size customer (200 nodes):
- Planning & approvals: 1 week
- Canary & verification: 1 week
- Progressive conversion: 2 weeks
- Sunset cutover: scheduled 48 hours
- Post-cleanup & audit: 4 weeks

Open questions / Next actions (for this doc):
- Draft customer-facing migration FAQ and required customer approvals (owner: Priya)
- Prepare automation that creates TF migration.tf imports from current state (owner: Runtime eng)
- Schedule dry-run migration for staging partner region

This is a working doc; please add notes inline. When converting from in_review to final, include the validated TF import script and a signed customer-approval template.
